case_name: Moru Venkatesh vs The State Of Ap
facts_of_case: Petitioner and his wife are living separately. Petitioner filed a petition for restitution of conjugal rights. Respondent police tried to arrest petitioner without following procedure.

legal_principles.principle: The police must follow the procedure prescribed under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C and guidelines issued by the Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar's case.
legal_principles.held: However, it is the contention of learned counsel for petitioner that while the investigation is pending, the 3rd respondent is bound to follow the procedure prescribed under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C and guidelines issued by Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar's case.
cited_cases: Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 2 SCC 1
use_in: cases involving police investigations and arrests

legal_principles.principle: The police must not arrest a person without following the procedure prescribed under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the petitioner seeks direction against the 3rd respondent to follow procedure under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C and guidelines issued by Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar's case.
cited_cases: Arnesh Kumar vs. State of Bihar, (2014) 2 SCC 1
use_in: cases involving police arrests and investigations

outcome.final_order: Court directed respondent police to follow procedure under Section 41-A of Cr.P.C and guidelines issued by Apex Court in Arnesh Kumar's case.
